newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan bolivar slips as Central Bank buys dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan bolivar slips as Central Bank buys dlrs.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar plunged to 473.00/474.00 per dollar Thursday, compared to 468.75/470.00 per dollar Wednesday, as the Central Bank entered the market in the afternoon to buy foreign currency, traders said.
The bank's decision to buy currency confused traders given its apparent policy of maintaining a strong bolivar.
"The Central Bank entered buying up dollars and the rate shot up. We don't understand why it changed its policy," one trader said.

One trader said the Central Bank was testing the sensitivity of the market. "It has spent weeks selling (foreign currency) and observing how the price behaves and suddenly it wants to see how the market unravels and measure its sensitivity," he said.

Traders said the market will be waiting to see what the Central Bank decides to do tomorrow but doubted that it would allow the exchange rate to fall as low as Thursday's opening around 468 bolivars per dollar again.
